description: How a node's identity becomes a fingerprint, and what the Master signs. Both roles must agree on this byte-for-byte or they will not validate each other. The reference implementation is shared/sparknet-authz.py; this file is the normative statement of the same rules.
identity_fields_note: Deliberately excludes hostname, vault path and timestamps: those change without changing identity, and including them would force a re-sign after a routine rename.
role_note: 'peer' is the working-node role. Both roles use the same identity schema; only the Master holds the signing key.

canonicalisation.projection: Keep only identity_fields, sorted by key.
canonicalisation.rationale: The bytes must not depend on dict insertion order or Python formatting differences, or the same identity would fingerprint differently on the two nodes.

fingerprint.input: canonical bytes of the projected identity
fingerprint.correction: WireGuard has no SHA-256 in its protocol. SHA-256 here is the authorization fingerprint; Ed25519 is what signs it. Describing this as 'SHA-256 WireGuard authentication' is wrong.

signed_envelope_note: Signing only the identity would leave capabilities and overlay_ipv4 mutable by anyone who can edit the registry file, escalating a node to guard-apply without the Master approving it. revoked is inside the envelope so only the Master can flip it.

registry.author: master
registry.distribution: UNSPECIFIED — the channel by which a signed registry reaches peers is not yet built. Peers currently read a local copy.
registry.empty_by_default_rationale: No node gets privileges by default. The shipped registry has no entries on purpose, so a fresh deployment is fail-closed.

master_public_key.format: base64 of a 32-byte Ed25519 public key
master_public_key.tracked_rationale: A public key is safe to track and must be, since peers need it to verify.
master_public_key.shipped_value_status: BOOTSTRAP ONLY — generated for structure; the private key was discarded, so it cannot sign anything. Real provisioning must generate a Master keypair and replace this value.

master_private_key.note: Never leaves the Master. Its absence on a peer is the whole trust boundary; verify this with `make authz-verify`, which must pass using the public key alone.
